subject: general
question: Who set up a Dayanand Anglo Vedic school in Lahore?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lala Lajpat Rai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was one of the prominent leaders of the Indian independence movement, known as the "Punjab Kesari" or "Lion of Punjab."
 
• He established the Dayanand Anglo Vedic (DAV) School in Lahore in 1886 as part of his efforts to promote education and social reform.
 
• The DAV School was founded under the influence of the Arya Samaj movement, which sought to promote Vedic education and social upliftment.
 
• The institution aimed to blend traditional Indian education based on Vedic principles with modern Western educational methods.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai emphasized education as a tool for empowerment and national awakening during the colonial period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arya Samaj:**

 
 
• A socio-religious reform movement founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875.
 
• Aimed to revive Vedic knowledge and culture while opposing social evils like caste discrimination and child marriage.
 
• Promoted education, especially for women, and emphasized Sanskrit as a medium of learning.
 
 
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai's Contributions:**
 
 
• Played a key role in the Swadeshi movement and was an advocate for boycotting British goods.
 
• He was a member of the Indian National Congress and later became associated with the extremist faction.
 
• Led protests against the Simon Commission in 1928, during which he sustained injuries that later led to his death.
 
 
 
• **Dayanand Anglo Vedic (DAV) Institutions:**
 
 
• The DAV movement expanded to establish schools and colleges across India, promoting education based on Arya Samaj principles.
 
• Currently, DAV institutions are among the largest chains of private educational institutions in India.
 
• Focuses on character building, spiritual growth, and academic excellence.
 
 
 
• **Education in Colonial India:**
 
 
• During British rule, education was largely limited to traditional systems and missionary schools.
 
• Indian leaders like Lala Lajpat Rai sought to create institutions that incorporated Indian values and modern education.
 
• Such initiatives contributed to the rise of nationalist consciousness among Indians.
